note: THE LEGEND (campaign/the-legend) is ratifying a GLYPH ALLOCATION RULE for the whole client and reserving codespace for the underworld, so Delving campaign 2 does not have to mint a second vocabulary. Context for whoever is heading down: three characters ALREADY collide across the client today, verified by reading every glyph constant. Dot is land in plate.rs:187, floor in plan.rs:69, and relief band 2 in surrounds_ascii:113. Plus is threshold in plan.rs:71, everything-else in chart.rs:79, and a water glyph in the sim. Hash is wall in plan.rs:67 and settlement in plate.rs:202. Only at-sign was ever assigned by rule and it is the only one all three panes agree on. THE RULE being ratified: a glyph carries ORDER (ink ascends with the quantity) or IDENTITY (the character is the referent initial), never an arbitrary category; colour carries category and may fail, so nothing a reader must trust lives only there; a character means ONE thing across the whole client, and two panes may use different ladders for different quantities but never the same character for two meanings. This is why the 22-biome set was rejected: the defect was NOMINALITY, not count, because ordinal marks self-legend and nominal marks never do. WHAT THIS MEANS FOR DELVING 2: an unallocated region is reserved for subterranean populations, so the cave chart CLAIMS from the register rather than inventing marks. If you need marks before The Legend lands, say so on the board and I will publish the register early rather than have you blocked.
